purpose: Record the first completed pilot source-specific extractions from the C2 long-tail first-batch queue. This register converts candidate sources into exact claim, endpoint, population, mechanism, uncertainty, transfer-boundary, downgrade and model-position fields while keeping calibrated modeling blocked.

currentLimitations: This is a pilot extraction register, not a complete first-batch Source Card set.
Rows are local source-context extractions and still require independent fresh review before card promotion.
No row admits calibrated prediction, intervention ranking, clinical advice or individual prognosis.

sourceAccessNotes: Publisher, society and government pages may block automated HTTP retrieval; URL accessibility is recorded as source-context metadata and does not itself upgrade or downgrade a scientific claim.
Guideline sources are used as route, endpoint and variable-definition anchors unless later fresh review extracts exact recommendation text, evidence grade, population and comparator.
Statistical-report and surveillance sources are used as burden and endpoint-context anchors, not causal-effect anchors.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for Acute Coronary Syndromes
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports treating ACS as a time-sensitive continuity failure mode where diagnosis, reperfusion, antithrombotic therapy, revascularization, rehabilitation and secondary prevention define the route variables to be extracted before any model use.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints include time-to-reperfusion, acute mortality, recurrent ischemic events, bleeding events, heart-failure transition, functional recovery and secondary-prevention adherence.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: People presenting with suspected or confirmed acute coronary syndrome across emergency medical services, emergency departments, inpatient cardiology and post-discharge care. Individual eligibility and treatment decisions remain outside this register.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism-level route signal: myocardial ischemia and thrombosis create a time-sensitive hazard channel; reperfusion and secondary prevention may alter acute risk, recurrent-event risk and functional reserve.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guidelines synthesize heterogeneous trials and evidence grades; local access, presentation delay, contraindications, bleeding risk and adherence can change transferability.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as endpoint, variable and care-pathway vocabulary. The source does not provide a calibrated Human Infra effect size or authorize personal ACS treatment advice.
downgradeTriggers: If a later card cannot extract recommendation class, evidence level, endpoint and comparator, keep as qualitative route support only.
If a claim jumps from guideline pathway to individual survival gain, downgrade to unsupported.
If bleeding, contraindication or access constraints are omitted, block intervention-ranking use.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: candidate endpoint and route definition only

extractedRows.nextAction: Create an ACS Source Card separating acute hazard reduction, post-event functional recovery, secondary prevention and access-delay variables.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: AHA Heart Disease and Stroke Statistics
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports ACS and cardiovascular disease as major burden domains for subject-continuity modeling by anchoring population-level event, mortality and risk-factor context.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Admissible endpoint language is limited to population burden, mortality, cardiovascular event categories and risk-factor context; this source does not define an intervention effect.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Population-level cardiovascular statistics, usually United States centered with selected global comparisons depending on the annual update section.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Burden-context signal only: the scale of cardiovascular events justifies ACS as a high-priority C2 continuity domain, but does not itself identify a causal intervention pathway.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Annual statistics combine surveillance systems, registry definitions and reporting conventions; endpoints may shift by year, coding source and population subgroup.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only to prioritization, endpoint vocabulary and denominator context. Do not use this source to estimate the benefit of reperfusion, medication or rehabilitation.
downgradeTriggers: If used as causal evidence for any intervention, downgrade to burden-context only.
If year, geography or endpoint definition is omitted, block quantitative parameter use.
If subgroup differences are ignored, require population-boundary review.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: domain priority and endpoint-context support only

extractedRows.nextAction: Extract the annual statistics sections into a burden card with year, geography, endpoint names and denominator definitions.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: Surviving Sepsis Campaign international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports treating sepsis and septic shock as acute systemic continuity failures where early recognition, antimicrobial therapy, source control, resuscitation and organ support define the route variables.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints include time-to-antibiotics, lactate or shock markers, organ dysfunction, vasopressor requirement, ICU survival, hospital mortality and post-sepsis functional burden.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Patients with suspected or confirmed sepsis or septic shock in emergency, ward and ICU settings. Later cards must separate adult, pediatric and setting-specific recommendations.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism-level route signal: infection-triggered dysregulated host response can produce organ dysfunction and shock; timely therapy and support may alter acute hazard and recovery trajectory.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guideline evidence is heterogeneous across infection sources, severity, age groups, health-system resources and recommendation strength; bundle timing can be confounded by severity and access.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only to route design, variables and endpoint vocabulary. Do not infer a personal sepsis prognosis or a calibrated Human Infra intervention effect from this register row.
downgradeTriggers: If adult and pediatric recommendations are mixed without boundary, downgrade to general route support.
If time-to-treatment is used without severity and setting context, block parameter admission.
If post-sepsis disability is omitted, require functional-burden extraction before continuity claims.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: candidate acute-hazard and recovery-route definition only

extractedRows.nextAction: Create separate sepsis cards for early recognition, antimicrobial timing, shock resuscitation, organ support and post-sepsis recovery.

extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports the public-health and clinical-context framing that sepsis requires rapid recognition, diagnostic evaluation, antimicrobial treatment and escalation when organ dysfunction or shock is suspected.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Admissible endpoints are presentation recognition, diagnostic workup, antimicrobial timing, escalation to emergency or critical care, survival and post-acute burden.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: General healthcare professional context for people with suspected sepsis across clinical settings; not a trial population and not an individual diagnostic rule.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Context signal: sepsis is framed as a medical emergency with infection, organ dysfunction and time-sensitive treatment pathways.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Public-health pages simplify evidence and may omit recommendation grades, comparators and detailed populations; they are not substitutes for full clinical guidelines.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only as public-health route context and vocabulary. Do not use as calibrated effect evidence, diagnostic advice or treatment instruction.
downgradeTriggers: If treated as a clinical protocol without guideline extraction, downgrade to context support.
If individual symptom interpretation is implied, block individual-advice use.
If ICU, post-acute or equity access boundaries are missing, keep model admission blocked.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: public-health clinical-context support only

extractedRows.nextAction: Pair with guideline and cohort evidence before any sepsis hazard or recovery parameter is proposed.

extractedRows.sourceTitle: KDIGO Acute Kidney Injury guideline hub
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports AKI as a continuity domain where definition, staging, risk prediction, nephrotoxin stewardship, fluid/hemodynamic management, kidney replacement therapy and follow-up define the route variables.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints include AKI stage, need for kidney replacement therapy, fluid balance, acute mortality, kidney recovery, CKD transition and long-term adverse kidney or cardiovascular outcomes.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: People at risk for, or experiencing, acute kidney disease or injury across hospital, ICU, procedure, medication and post-discharge contexts. Later cards must separate pediatric/adult and critical-care boundaries.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism-level route signal: acute renal filtration and homeostasis failure can alter fluid, electrolyte, acid-base, medication-safety and multi-organ risk channels.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guideline hubs contain definitions and recommendations but not a single effect estimate; biomarker use, e-alerts, KRT timing and modality depend on setting and evidence strength.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only to AKI variable, staging and route vocabulary. Do not use as proof that a specific AKI intervention improves lifespan or effective time.
downgradeTriggers: If AKI stage, baseline creatinine and follow-up horizon are absent, block quantitative use.
If KRT timing or modality is treated as universally beneficial, downgrade to route hypothesis.
If CKD transition and medication-toxicity boundaries are omitted, keep as qualitative support.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: candidate renal-failure state and transition vocabulary only

extractedRows.nextAction: Extract KDIGO AKI definition, staging, KRT and follow-up cards with separate endpoint and population boundaries.

extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Admissible endpoint language includes AKI hospitalization, dialysis-requiring AKI, mortality, kidney recovery and later CKD or kidney-failure transition when the report defines them.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Population-level surveillance and administrative-data context, not an intervention cohort and not an individual risk calculator.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Burden-context signal: AKI is a high-impact acute-to-chronic transition state that can affect survival, treatment safety and long-term organ reserve.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Administrative definitions, coding changes, hospitalization selection and dialysis definitions can change measured burden and apparent outcomes.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only to burden, endpoint naming and transition-context framing. Do not infer causal effects of fluids, drugs, dialysis timing or individual prognosis.
downgradeTriggers: If surveillance definitions are omitted, block parameter use.
If AKI burden is treated as intervention effect evidence, downgrade to context only.
If kidney recovery and CKD transition horizons are mixed, require separate endpoint cards.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: burden and endpoint-context support only

extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports anaphylaxis as an acute continuity-risk domain where rapid recognition, epinephrine access, airway/circulation risk and emergency transfer define the route variables.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints include time-to-epinephrine, respiratory or cardiovascular compromise, recurrence or biphasic reaction risk, emergency-care access and acute survival.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: People with suspected anaphylaxis across community, emergency, allergy and healthcare settings; individual trigger identification and action plans require clinical context outside this register.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism-level route signal: systemic allergic reaction can rapidly compromise airway, breathing and circulation; timely epinephrine and emergency response may alter acute hazard.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guidance documents combine consensus and evidence across triggers, ages and settings; access to epinephrine, education and emergency services strongly modifies route performance.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only to emergency route, endpoint and downgrade vocabulary. Do not use to advise an individual whether or how to administer medication.
downgradeTriggers: If epinephrine access, airway risk and emergency transfer are not separated, keep as route support.
If individual allergy diagnosis or medication instructions are implied, block individual-advice use.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: emergency-route and endpoint vocabulary only

extractedRows.sourceTitle: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for CKD Evaluation and Management
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports CKD as a chronic state-transition domain where eGFR, albuminuria, progression risk, cardiovascular risk and kidney-failure transition define core model variables.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints include CKD diagnosis/stage, eGFR slope, albuminuria category, cardiovascular events, kidney failure, renal replacement transition, mortality and quality-of-life burden.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: People with known or suspected CKD across primary care, nephrology and comorbidity-management settings. Later extraction must separate disease stage, diabetes, hypertension and age-group boundaries.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Mechanism-level route signal: chronic loss of filtration and albuminuric injury can alter cardiovascular risk, medication safety, treatment burden and long-term reserve.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Guideline recommendations depend on testing availability, staging definitions, comorbidity, risk equations, medication access and evidence grade.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only to CKD state, staging, progression and endpoint vocabulary. Do not use as an individual kidney-risk calculator or treatment recommendation.
downgradeTriggers: If eGFR and albuminuria categories are not specified, block model parameter use.
If CKD progression is inferred without horizon and population, downgrade to qualitative state support.
If cardiovascular and kidney outcomes are merged, require separate endpoint cards.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: candidate chronic kidney state and transition vocabulary only

extractedRows.sourceTitle: WHO Obesity and overweight fact sheet
extractedRows.exactClaimUse: Supports obesity and overweight as global burden and risk-context domains, including measurement vocabulary, disease-risk framing and population-level public-health relevance.
extractedRows.endpointDefinition: Candidate endpoints include BMI category, overweight or obesity prevalence, metabolic disease burden, cardiovascular disease burden, musculoskeletal burden and population-level risk-factor context when defined by the source.
extractedRows.populationOrSetting: Global population and public-health setting. The source is not a clinical trial, not an individual body-composition assessment and not a personalized weight-loss protocol.
extractedRows.effectOrMechanismSignal: Burden and mechanism-context signal: excess adiposity is linked with noncommunicable disease risk, metabolic stress, mechanical load and health-system burden, but this extraction does not quantify individual causal effects.
extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: BMI does not directly measure fat distribution, body composition or individual metabolic health; country, age, sex, ethnicity, survey method and diagnostic threshold affect transferability.
extractedRows.transferBoundary: Transfer only to global burden framing, endpoint vocabulary and risk-channel identification. Do not infer personal prognosis, treatment ranking or calibrated adiposity-risk effects.
downgradeTriggers: If BMI is treated as a complete body-composition measure, downgrade to measurement-context only.
If prevalence or burden is transferred across countries, age groups or years without denominator review, block quantitative use.
If the source is used to rank obesity interventions, block and require intervention-specific evidence.

modelPosition.admissibleUse: global burden and endpoint vocabulary only

extractedRows.uncertaintyOrBias: Fitness estimates vary by direct measurement versus estimation, protocol, age, sex, medication, comorbidity, disability, baseline activity and selection into testing.
